newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TIGER OATS SEES GROWTH IN TOUGH MARKETS.
newsitem.headline: TIGER OATS SEES GROWTH IN TOUGH MARKETS.

text.p: South African diversified foods group Tiger Oats Ltd said on Tuesday that it was set to achieve further earnings growth in 1997 despite operating in tough markets.

"Trading conditions are likely to remain challenging in the coming year. But provided consumer demand does not weaken significantly, further real growth in earnings will be achieved," the firm said in a statement with its year results.
Earlier the firm posted a 25 percent rise in headline earnings per share to 372.2 cents, way above analysts' forecast range of 344-351 cents.
The firm, which also has interests in the drugs industry, said headline earnings jumped 28 percent in its core foods businesses.
The firm was hit by poor results in its poultry operations, but these were offset by healthy showings from the group's rice, canned fruit and vegetable, maize and wheat units.
Unlisted wholesaling operation Spar also performed well, despite a rash of new entrants into its markets, the firm said.
Tiger Oats has this year bought a 50 percent slice of malting venture ConAgra Inc of the United States and a 19 percent stake in another U.S firm, frozen seafood group Van de Kamp's.
"These acquisitions will not have a material effect on the earnings of the Tiger Oats in the short term, but have significant growth potential over the medium and long term," the firm said.

The group's drugs unit, newly merged Adcock Ingram Ltd, posted results on Monday and saw headline earnings per share rise 3.4 percent to 98.2 cents after a 107 percent dilution of its share capital following its takeover of former rival Premier.
